Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-14
Start: 09:15 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lucia Gomez (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NexaHealth CTO), Rajiv Singh (Nexa ML Eng), Priya Patel (Nexa Infra), Alex (Nexa PM)

Auto Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um let's do quick intros, I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on this deal. Lucia is our systems engineer.
[00:08] Lucia: hi all, hey, Luci-ia here, I'll be driving the bench test and the tuning.
[00:13] Maya: Hi, Maya here, thanks. I've got Rajiv and Priya on the call, and Alex.
[00:18] Rajiv: morning.
[00:20] Priya: good morning.
[00:22] Samir: Cool, agenda — short sync: 1) onboarding status 2) results review (small-run we did last week) 3) tuning next steps 4) compliance/access remaining items, and 5) schedule. Sound good?
[00:36] Alex: yep good.
[00:38] Samir: Lucia, you want to kick off with the benchmark recap?
[00:41] Lucia: Sure. Quick recap — last Thursday we ran the 5k token end-to-end test on the staging environment you gave us, the one behind the temporary peering. The run showed median latency of about 320ms per request for the 2k token profile and tail out to 780ms for a 5k context when we enforced synchronous calls. There was some variability because we hit a small spikes on the KV cache misses — I suspect the prefix cache wasn't primed for a few of the sequences.
[01:10] Rajiv: yeah we saw that on our side too, some requests looked slow, maybe the cache warming. I also noticed the GPU utilization was a bit lower than expected, about 62% avg. Might be batch sizing.
[01:22] Lucia: exactly, batch size and the batching window were conservative. For the bench run we used continuous batching window of 30ms which for your QPS ended up producing 2-3 token batches. If we relax to 80-100ms we should see better GPU utilization and lower token cost but a little higher P95 latency. It's the usual tradeoff.
[01:41] Samir: important to quantify that for your SLOs — Maya, what are the latency targets you need for production?
[01:46] Maya: Ideally sub-400ms median for the 2k profile. Some of our UX flows are latency-sensitive; the 5k contexts we can accept up to 1.2s p95. But cost matters a lot too, so we need the balance.
[01:59] Samir: Great. So the options are: hosted API for quick launch, Redwood Dedicated for reserved capacity and lower jitter, or Redwood Private if you need VPC/on-prem. Mary — uh Maya — you've been leaning dedicated?
[02:12] Maya: yes, we're leaning dedicated because of predictable throughput and compliance; we also want better control over encryption keys via KMS. But we need to see the numbers.
[02:21] Samir: Understood. Lucia, status on the tuning plan?
[02:24] Lucia: I'll run two cycles: 1) quick batching sweep (30ms, 60ms, 100ms windows) to show latency vs cost curve, 2) KV cache priming and prefix caching tests to improve cold-starts. Also plan to try a quantized variant on the same GPU instance class to measure token throughput delta. Should have initial numbers by Friday.
[02:47] Rajiv: a question on the quantized variant — will that affect the quality of completions for our safety prompts and classification tasks? We have strict quality criteria.
[02:55] Lucia: Good question. Generally 8-bit quantization has small quality delta; we'll include your eval prompt set in the bench and compare BLEU/accuracy on the evals. If there's regression we'll flag it.
[03:06] Maya: Are there any concerns around inference fallbacks? Like if dedicated pool is saturated, what happens?
[03:12] Samir: Redwood supports smart routing and fallbacks — we can route to a compatible model variant or to hosted capacity as a buffer. Fallback policy can be configured per-route. We'll share the routing policy doc.
[03:22] Priya: On my side, the blocker is we haven't finalized VPC peering and the JIT bastion access — our security team needs SAML SSO and audit log hooks. We also need to verify SOC2 evidence.
[03:34] Samir: For SSO we support SAML/Okta and SCIM provisioning; audit logs and KMS integrations are standard for Private and Dedicated. I'll attach the SOC2 and security pack after this call.
[03:47] Priya: Great. Also, can we confirm that Redwood's KMS integration supports external HSM? Our compliance team requires HSM-backed keys.
[03:56] Lucia: We support customer-managed KMS and there are HSM options — I'll include the specifics and any limitations depending on the deployment mode. For Private it's straightforward; Dedicated we can integrate with your KMS via IAM roles.
[04:10] Rajiv: quick technical: when you say KV cache misses caused latency spikes, is that because of cold-start of embeddings or because of cache eviction?
[04:18] Lucia: Mostly because the prefix cache wasn't primed. In the bench we used a small working set so some sequences missed the cache; eviction is possible at very high concurrency, but not what we saw. Priming and sticky routing will reduce that.
[04:31] Alex: we also want to capture cost per 1k tokens for our finance team. Can you give a rough delta between hosted and dedicated?
[04:40] Samir: Roughly speaking, dedicated reduces per-token cost by 20-40% depending on utilization and batching. We'll run concrete numbers after Lucia's bench. I'll include a pricing worksheet in the follow-up.
[04:51] Maya: On security docs: we'll need the encryption-at-rest details, retention periods, and any subprocessor list.
[04:58] Samir: Yep, security pack will include that.
[05:00] Lucia: For the bench next steps, I need 1) VPC peering confirmed, 2) a test user with SAML or SSH bastion, and 3) the eval prompt set. Rajiv, can you share the prompt set or a sanitized version?
[05:12] Rajiv: yes, I can share the sanitized evals by EOD tomorrow. There may be some PII in the real prompts so we'll sanitize.
[05:18] Priya: I'll share the peering and subnet details by Monday. Also need to coordinate with our security lead for the SOC2 docs.
[05:25] Samir: Sounds good. One small note — during the bench we saw a library (tokenizer) mismatch on one node which led to a couple malformed tokens in the trace. That was our staging artifact but we want to avoid in prod.
[05:37] Lucia: Right, we'll standardize the runtime/container image and include the exact versions in the runbook.
[05:43] Alex: timeline question — if tuning goes well, what does a fast pilot-to-prod path look like? Weeks?
[05:50] Samir: Typical is 4–6 weeks from POC to pilot depending on compliance gating and peering. If peering and SOC2 evidence are quick, could be accelerated.
[05:59] Maya: fine. Any other blockers?
[06:01] Priya: none from infra beyond what's discussed.
[06:04] Rajiv: just want to ensure we get the eval metrics for quality with quantized model.
[06:08] Lucia: will include BLEU/accuracy/F1 on your eval set plus token-level diffs.
[06:14] Samir: ok let's recap and next steps.
[06:17] Samir: Next steps: Samir to send pricing + security pack; Lucia to run batching/quant bench and send tuning checklist; Nexa provides peering, sanitized evals, and confirms stakeholders.
[06:30] Maya: Thanks everyone, that works.
[06:33] Samir: Thanks, we'll follow up via email and Slack.
[06:36] (call ends)
